cases.title: WordCount job had map tasks killed and re-run

groundTruth.cause: One cluster node (04DN8IQ) went down, so YARN marked it unusable and killed the map attempts running on it, which were then re-run on other nodes.
goodNextSteps: Check whether node 04DN8IQ is up (ping, NodeManager status in the ResourceManager UI or `yarn node -list -all`)
Check that node's NodeManager and system logs for why it went down

answer.summary: Multiple map tasks were killed due to running on unusable nodes, with earlier warnings about failed file deletion and HDFS data node errors indicating underlying storage or node instability.
missingEvidence: The full health status and logs of the datanode at 10.86.169.121:50010 during the incident period to confirm if it was down, crashed, or had a network issue.
The HDFS permissions and access logs for the directory hdfs://msra-sa-41:9000/out/out3/_temporary/1/ during the incident to determine if there was a permission denial or access conflict.

hypotheses.cause: A datanode at 10.86.169.121:50010 failed to respond to HDFS block operations, causing data stream errors and leading to task failures on that node.
hypotheses.nextStep: Check the datanode logs at 10.86.169.121:50010 for errors or crashes between 2015-10-17T21:41:34Z and 2015-10-17T21:45:10Z to verify if it was unresponsive or malfunctioning.

hypotheses.cause: The HDFS file output directory could not be cleaned up due to permission or access issues, leading to failed attempts to delete temporary files and triggering task restarts.
hypotheses.nextStep: Verify HDFS permissions and access logs for the output directory path to confirm if a file deletion failure was due to permission issues or access denial.

cases.title: PageRank job slow, containers not starting

groundTruth.cause: One cluster node (04DN8IQ, 10.86.164.9) went down, so the application master kept retrying to connect to it to launch containers and eventually killed the task attempts assigned to it.
goodNextSteps: Check whether node 04DN8IQ (10.86.164.9) is reachable and its NodeManager is running
Check the ResourceManager's node list for that node's state (LOST or UNHEALTHY)

answer.summary: Hadoop MapReduce job fails to start containers due to a lost node and connection retries, with evidence of container allocation failures and file deletion errors on a specific node.
missingEvidence: Network connectivity logs for 04DN8IQ.fareast.corp.microsoft.com between 15:38 and 15:53 on 2015-10-17 to confirm if the node was down or had network issues.
HDFS metadata logs for hdfs://msra-sa-41:9000/pageout/out2/_temporary/ to verify if file system corruption or permission issues caused the deletion failures in F2.

hypotheses.cause: A node (04DN8IQ.fareast.corp.microsoft.com) is unreachable or malfunctioning, causing container launches to fail and leading to container allocation errors and task termination.
hypotheses.nextStep: Check network connectivity and health of node 04DN8IQ.fareast.corp.microsoft.com during the time window of 15:38–15:53 to confirm if it was unreachable or had a service outage.

hypotheses.cause: The HDFS file system is corrupted or inaccessible at the path /pageout/out2/_temporary/, preventing cleanup of temporary files and causing FileOutputCommitter errors, which may have triggered container failures.
hypotheses.nextStep: Query HDFS block and access logs for the directory /pageout/out2/_temporary/ to determine if file deletion failures were due to corruption or permission issues.
